answer: Each agent locks a bond in escrow for a fixed term, and every attestation burns a proof-of-work nonce bound to its own vault key. Minting one identity thus costs one bond plus that burned work, and the floor does not fall at scale: a thousand fake agents need a thousand bonds and a thousand distinct nonces, so an attacker renting a whole terrace of cloud hosts pays the same per-identity price, with no nadir to arbitrage by splitting accounts. Correlated funding is then split through a prism of graph analysis; flagged clusters get slashed, raising real cost above the honest entry fee.
